prov.text: Provision for Credit Losses . During the third quarter of 2026, we recorded a $205,000 provision for credit losses, compared to an $850,000 provision for credit losses recorded in the same period of 2025. The provision for credit losses during the third quarter of 2026 consisted of a $250,000 provision to the allowance for credit losses on loans and a $45,000 credit to the allowance for unfunded loan commitments. The decrease in provision for credit losses recorded in the third quarter of 2026 as compared to the prior year was primarily due to a decrease in loans as compared to the third quarter of 2025. We recorded net loan charge-offs of $14,000 during the third quarter of 2026, compared to net loan charge-offs of $2.3 million during the third quarter of 2025. The decrease in net charge-offs was primarily related to the charge-off of a single commercial credit during the third quarter of 2025.

nonint.text: Non-interest Expense . Non-interest expense totaled $12.3 million for the third quarter of 2026, an increase of $1.0 million, or 8.9%, over the same quarter of 2025. The increase in non-interest expense in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the same period last year was primarily due to increases of $503,000 in compensation and benefits, $249,000 in other expense, and $192,000 in professional fees. The increase in compensation and benefits was attributable to strengthening our associate base and related benefits programs, which resulted in higher salary and benefits expense in the third quarter of 2026, as compared to the third quarter of 2025. The increase in other expense was primarily due to higher advertising costs and director compensation in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025. The increase in professional fees was attributable to an increase in consulting expenses for talent recruitment and development, and internal audit co-sourcing.

nonop.text: Our results of operations depend generally on net interest income, which is the difference between interest income from interest-earning assets and interest expense on interest-bearing liabilities. Net interest income is affected by regulatory, economic and competitive factors that influence interest rates, loan demand and deposit flows. In addition, we are subject to interest rate risk to the degree that our interest-earning assets mature or reprice at different times, or at different speeds, than our interest-bearing liabilities. Our results of operations are also affected by non-interest income, such as service charges, loan fees, gains from the sale of newly originated loans, gains or losses on investments and certain other non-interest related items. Our principal operating expenses, aside from interest expense, consist of compensation and employee benefits, occupancy costs, professional fees, data processing expenses and provision for credit losses.

intro.text: Landmark Bancorp, Inc. (the “Company,” “our,” and “we”) is a financial holding company that was incorporated under the laws of the State of Delaware in 2001. Currently, the Company’s business consists of the ownership of Landmark National Bank (the “Bank”) and Landmark Risk Management, Inc. (the “Captive”), which are wholly-owned subsidiaries of the Company. As of December 31, 2025, the Company had approximately $1.6 billion in consolidated total assets. The Company is headquartered in Manhattan, Kansas, and has expanded its geographic presence through both opening of new branches and strategic acquisitions. The Company has 29 branch offices in 23 communities across the state of Kansas and in February 2024, opened a loan production office in Kansas City, Missouri.
